## Identity

Name: Mohammad Raouf Abedini (Raouf)
Role: AI Security Researcher · Adversarial Robustness & AI Control · Empirical Safety Evaluation
Location: Sydney · Relocating to San Francisco, CA · Visa sponsorship required
Availability: Full-time from December 2026 for a three- to six-month San Francisco placement
Focus: Host-side authorisation for tool-using AI agents, matched-control safety evaluation, adversarial robustness and AI control.

## Summary

Security researcher focused on keeping tool-using AI agents safe and beneficial: builds host-side controls for what an agent is permitted to do and stress-tests them with matched-control experiments against live models. Sole author of Project Simurgh, an open-source agent-authorization prototype whose October 2026 study reports a benefit on one model and a null result on another (no incremental protection on gpt-6-luna). Evaluated Claude for exploitable code and guardrail circumvention in Anthropic's safety-evaluation program via Alignerr. Five sole-author preprints and two coordinated vendor disclosures (Microsoft, Apple) after seven years in security operations and engineering. Available full-time from December 2026 for a three- to six-month San Francisco placement.

## Research & Technical Skills

- Empirical AI safety and alignment: matched-control experiment design · adversarial robustness and AI control for tool-using agents · prompt-injection and authority containment · guardrail and classifier evaluation · uncertainty reporting · host-held human-oversight state (delegation, stop, lease)
- Large language models (LLMs) and agent tooling: Claude API and Claude Code · OpenAI Responses API with tool calling · self-hosted Llama (3.2-3B, 3.3-70B) · Llama Guard 4 · AgentDojo · MCP servers
- AI security, safeguards and red-teaming: guardrail-circumvention analysis · red-team scenario design · vulnerability research and coordinated disclosure · offensive proofs of concept · intrusion detection · phishing-detection ML · incident response · MITRE ATT&CK
- Languages and systems: Python · TypeScript · C · C++17/20 · Rust · Kotlin · Lean 4 · SQL · Bash · Docker · GitHub Actions · PostgreSQL · Linux · eBPF

## Featured Research & Projects

1. Project Simurgh (FLAGSHIP): Inspectable Authorization and Containment for AI Agents (Sole Author), May 2026 – Present; 92 releases. Transfer study (Oct 2026): 24 tasks, two trials each, three matched controls (credential-only, composed, deny-all) and two models; 288 replayed branches. On Meta Llama-3.2-3B, composed host controls cut restricted-state trials with new effects from 17/24 to 0/24, kept 23/24 useful completions and blocked no valid proposal. On OpenAI gpt-6-luna the baseline was already 0/24, so the study reports no incremental protection there. Wilson 95% per-state intervals: 43.6–97.0% versus 0.0–39.0%; part of the gap holds by construction. OpenAI integration defect: role-placement error (8/8 declined); a frozen developer-role correction completed 2/3 authorized workflows and declined 5/5 restricted ones, with one refusal still open. Llama Guard 4 12B (180-case set): containment evidence for all 138 malicious cases it missed, 120 of them downstream injections. AgentDojo: live Llama-3.3-70B targeted attack success 9/140 to 0/140 (workspace suite); full four-suite deterministic run 0/949 attack success with 949/949 unattacked utility (both scoped as small experiments). Ed25519-signed evidence archives replay offline in one command; 39 Lean 4 proofs sit behind a gate that fails on any unproven “sorry” placeholder; 5,171 tests passed in the 19 Oct 2026 smoke run. Software DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21737792; device-integrity preprint DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20374849.
2. The Invisible Window: Screen-Capture Evasion in WebRTC Proctoring (Sole Author), Feb 2026 – May 2026. Documented display-affinity APIs on Windows and macOS let a window stay visible on the monitor while contributing zero pixels to screen capture: 100% evasion of WebRTC proctoring on every platform tested, including macOS 26. Disclosed to Microsoft MSRC (Feb 2026) and Apple Product Security (Mar 2026) before publication; both classified the behavior as by design. Proof-of-concept code is withheld on dual-use grounds. IEEE-format preprint v2.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20376495.
3. Aion-BibleQA: Retrieval and Citation Faithfulness in a RAG System (Sole Author), Jun 2026. Built and scored a 40-question benchmark for retrieval quality, citation support and false-premise robustness: R@5 of 0.941, mean citation support of 0.978, zero unsupported citations and 6/6 false-premise refusals. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20522874.
4. Project Zurvan: local-first knowledge engine serving claims and decisions to agents over MCP (218 tests).
5. Syllabus-Sync: Macquarie University Incubator startup (cofounder). Led the security backend (WebAuthn passkeys, TOTP MFA, Postgres row-level security, tamper-resistant audit logging) of a shared Next.js/TypeScript codebase that converts university syllabi into structured data; 503 tests across 92 files. https://syllabus-sync.app
6. Mehr Guard: offline QR and URL phishing scanner in Kotlin Multiplatform; ensemble ML plus 25 heuristics at 87% F1 and under 5 ms, 19-scenario red-team mode.
7. SentinelFlow: C++17 intrusion detection (500,000+ packets/sec, synthetic single-thread benchmark).
8. NanoMatch: C++20 matching engine. Repository reports 9.29M mixed add/cancel operations/s over 5M synthetic operations, single thread, Apple M-series Release build. Order-ID lookup is expected O(1); end-to-end cancellation includes an O(log M) price-level lookup. Reported insertion-latency percentiles time add_order, not cancellation; the standalone pool benchmark is not a zero-allocation hot-path guarantee.
9. ECRSM: Defensive educational eBPF/perf-event/Go/SSE/React scaffold. The current Go entrypoint loads the event map but does not attach the kernel hooks; complete live capture is not established. Helm deployment is privileged and uses hostPID and BPF/SYS_ADMIN/SYS_PTRACE capabilities; this is not a capabilities-only least-privilege deployment.
10. GitSwitch: Multi-identity Git client with declared Electron 39/React 19 dependencies. Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, local-model and offline commit generation. Main-process safeStorage encrypts credential files when available; cloud consent/redaction and bounded requests are implemented. JavaScript reference clearing is best effort, not secure memory erasure.
11. Divan Open Day: English/Persian poetry experience for a Persian Society stall. Verified release/cache state enables offline use. Application code has no visitor form, tracking cookies or analytics endpoint; hosting/network connection data is a separate boundary. The July 2026 corpus report records 60 Hafez and 60 Rumi records; this is not cultural or manual accessibility certification.
12. Nexus Archive: React/Litestar/Supabase media vault and job tracker. Takeaway-note Fernet encryption requires configuration. Backend HttpOnly cookies coexist with browser-visible bearer tokens; no whole-app frontend-token-isolation claim is made. CI definitions are evidence of configured checks, not a demonstrated green HEAD run.
13. SimurghForge: Tauri v2/Rust/React 19 local file converter with 9 engine variants. CLI-backed conversions require installed tools. Backend limits: 50 files and 1–8 concurrent jobs. Supported conversions depend on the input/output pair and available engines; no blanket 49-format guarantee is asserted.

14. FORMA: Workout planner with custom routines, set logging, workout history, member accounts and a separate local guest mode. React, TypeScript, Vite, PostgreSQL and Cloudflare Workers. Native SwiftUI iPhone, Apple Watch and widget projects are in development, not published App Store releases. https://forma.raoufabedini.dev · https://raoufabedini.dev/projects/forma
15. SentinelSSH: Rust MCP gateway with 17 typed, read-only inspection tools for registered Linux hosts. Observer-mode development release; gateway policy is not a remote sandbox. https://github.com/Raoof128/sentinel-ssh · https://raoufabedini.dev/projects/sentinel-ssh
16. Gmail MCP: Multi-account Gmail server with server-enforced allow/ask/deny policy and attachment transfers through a local companion. Pre-release; five external qualification gates remain open. https://github.com/Raoof128/gmail-mcp · https://raoufabedini.dev/projects/gmail-mcp

## Professional Experience

- AI Safety Evaluator (Claude) — Alignerr, Jan 2026 – Mar 2026. Anthropic safety-evaluation program · Remote. Stress-tested Claude's safety guardrails: assessed outputs for exploitable code and harmful patterns, analyzed circumvention methods, and delivered rubric-based findings.
- Cofounder — Syllabus-Sync, May 2026 – Present. Macquarie University Incubator startup · Sydney · syllabus-sync.app. Led the security backend (WebAuthn passkeys, TOTP MFA, Postgres row-level security, tamper-resistant audit logging) of a shared Next.js/TypeScript codebase that converts university syllabi into structured data; 503 tests across 92 files.
- Security Engineer & Full-Stack Developer — Self-Employed (Freelance), Jan 2024 – Present. Sydney. Delivered secure web applications for commercial clients with OWASP Top 10 controls and OAuth 2.0; 5.0-star rating across 31 Airtasker reviews.
- IT Manager & Security Operations — Iran Pharmacy, Aug 2019 – Jan 2024. 50+ staff · Iran. Investigated unauthorized-access incidents, built automated detection workflows that cut manual triage by about 30%, and enforced least-privilege access.

## Further systems work

- SentinelSSH: a Rust MCP server that gives AI agents policy-scoped, read-only inspection of Linux hosts through 17 typed tools and no shell.

## Approach

Privacy by design, local-first processing and security from design through deployment. Current work tests host-side authorisation controls for tool-using AI agents and publishes null results alongside positive ones.
